Subject: Fwd: Renewal: structuring growth acceleration & bucketization

Marissa / Ben / Naomi —

Forwarding Ainsley's usage export and request. Key asks from Helix: co-term to 2029-12-31 and a short runway to absorb a sustained growth profile. They prefer minimal procurement friction (PO + single amendment).

Considerations I raised on call:
- Hybrid approach: keep base committed capacity at current rates, add a 6–9 month accelerator bucket (prepaid at a modest uplift) that auto-converts to committed capacity if consumed above threshold.
- Voucher/top-up vs. blended uplift: vouchers are operationally simple but more expensive; blended uplift smooths billing and is better for forecasting.
- Discount triggers: if they hit >120% of forecasted Q over two consecutive months, we reduce uplift on marginal units and convert some usage into committed capacity with a retroactive credit.

Can the pricing team run a 3-scenario sheet: conservative (vouchers only), blended (50/50 voucher+uplift), conversion (prepaid bucket with auto-convert)? I've attached a placeholder pricing sheet for numbers (pricingsheet_v2.xlsx).

Also capture contract/ops asks: single amendment, DocuSign-ready, procurement PO window of 45 days.

Thx — Priyom
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Mar 2028 08:56:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal: structuring growth acceleration & bucketization

Team —

Attached is a pricing sketch with the three scenarios Priyom asked for. Highlights:
- Conservative (vouchers): 20% uplift on top-up blocks, immediate invoicing, no retro credits.
- Blended: 10% uplift on the accelerator bucket, 8% credit if conversion triggers inside 6 months.
- Conversion-first: 6% uplift with auto-conversion when run-rate sustains for 2 months; applies a retroactive credit equal to difference between voucher price and committed price for the converted volume.

I modeled Helix's current run-rate and the 35% MoM spike. Net-present-value favors blended for both revenue predictability and customer unit economics.

Attachments: pricingsheet_v2.xlsx (xlsx)

If legal needs a simpler clause for auto-convert, keep the trigger definition narrow (sustained run-rate and mutual notice).

—Ben
Director, Growth Sales Operations
